title: Home-worktree identity is derived from the mutable branch string, so a home worktree on any other branch stops being home
description:
Found during the THE-706 reader audit (2026-09-29); deliberately excluded from that issue because reconciling it against git would make it worse.

`crates/thegn-host/src/attention_status.rs` (~:126):
```rust
meta.insert(wt.worktree.clone(), Meta { slug, is_home: wt.branch == "home", position: wt.position, repo: wt.repo_root.clone() });
```
Whether a worktree is the HOME worktree is decided by string-comparing the registry's `branch` column to the literal "home".

THE-706 made `worktrees.branch` reconcile against git. Applied here, a home worktree checked out on `main` (the normal case) would reconcile to `main` and stop satisfying `== "home"`. The bug is that a BRANCH NAME is used as a durable IDENTITY.

Consequences: `is_home` feeds attention/notification classification. A home worktree on any branch other than literal `home` is classified as ordinary, and any ordinary worktree on a branch named `home` is classified as home.

## Suggested direction
Use a stable identity, not a branch string. The row carries `tab_name`, `position`, `repo_root`, and the home worktree is a distinct concept in the workspace model — one of those (or an explicit flag) is the right source. Pick the authoritative one rather than adding a second heuristic. Also grep for other `branch == "home"`-style identity checks.

## Acceptance criteria
- Home-worktree classification does not read `worktrees.branch`.
- A home worktree checked out on `main` (or any branch) is still classified as home.
- An ordinary worktree on a branch named `home` is not classified as home.
- A test covers both directions.
